steps.title: The Filters palette
steps.body: Filters opens a palette for one layer. RHEF, the radial histogram equalizing filter, comes first and works frame by frame. Below it, the Fourier filter and the noise gate work over the whole movie.

steps.title: RHEF in the layer options
steps.body: Select a layer in the list and open Intensity: its Filter row is the same RHEF switch, bound to the same setting. When the tour starts on an empty canvas it loads the bundled SDO/AIA 171 sample, so there is a layer to try. The Υ button beside the list stays greyed until RHEF is chosen. Then it opens Shadows (Υ low) and Highlights (Υ high), which soften RHEF output below and above the median, each on its own; a curve that shows their shape; a Look menu; and Hold to compare, which shows that one layer without RHEF while you hold it.

steps.title: Reading an RHEF image
steps.body: RHEF output is a visualization, not a calibrated radiance. Measure on the original data, with the filter set to None. The method is described in Gilly & Cranmer 2025.

steps.title: Find a filter by name
steps.body: Help > Search Controls finds any control by name. Try noise gate, or RHEF.
